answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied leaders receive no coin and the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader still gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Census: tied lead gives no coin; unique last pays; in a 2-player game the last player never pays.

answers.answer: You do not have to draw six: you may draw any number up to the allowance, limited by free Market spaces, so at most two here. Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Followers: draw any number up to the allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but it activates only when all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs only one space). You may save an activated action for a later round. When executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Planning/Actions: actions may be filled gradually; activation requires all spaces except Town Hall; activation can be saved; after executing, return Followers to your bag and Technology stays.

answers.answer: Starting with the Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly, each taking one activated action or passing. Passing ends your participation for the Action Phase, so you cannot act again that round. Unused activations retain their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Actions: take one activated action or pass; passing ends your participation; unused activations keep their Followers for future rounds.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted on that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Farm House: put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.

answers.answer: Village lets you recruit one of a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader, putting the chosen neutral Follower in your bag and advancing that profession's track one space. Boatman gains the depicted coins (or a Citizen for the first player at the last space); Craftsman gains a Technology tile, usable only after passing; Trader gains one Place Tile, category I on the first advance and I or II on later advances.
answers.evidence: Actions → Village recruitment: each chosen neutral Follower enters your bag and its track advances; listed profession-specific rewards.

answers.answer: No. A newly gained Craftsman Technology can be used only after you pass, so it cannot help execute another action this round after that pass. Your first placed Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technology may replace any profession except Monk. Technology remains on its space, cannot be moved, and you may place no more than one at a Place or any at a Place requiring only one Follower.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment and Technology: Craftsman tile is used only after passing; first Technology replaces a Farmer; subsequent placement restrictions and permanence are stated.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only; every later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Setup: players may inspect Place Tile stacks at any time. Village recruitment: first Traders Track advance permits category I; later advances I or II.

answers.answer: University puts a Scholar in your bag, advances the Scholars Track, and gives its depicted Development Points. Castle puts a Knight in your bag and advances the Knights Track, which sets future draw allowance. Monastery puts a Monk in your bag with no extra track reward. Recruiting the fourth Knight does not raise the allowance above 7 at that step; once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Character-track limits: University/Castle/Monastery effects; fourth Knight does not raise allowance above 7; no further corresponding action at last space.

answers.answer: Yes, a Monk may replace a Knight on an ordinary action. No, a Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. No, Monks or other substitutions cannot replace the exact professions depicted on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Monks: Monk can replace any other profession in ordinary actions, but the reverse is forbidden. Town Hall: Deeds require exact professions; substitutions cannot replace them.

answers.answer: One Ship or Wagon action moves the Merchant along one adjacent Waterway or Road connection, respectively. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if multiple goods are there. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: one connection per action; one good at most; empty Roads/Waterways are legal and yield no good.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with another player's station cannot receive another station. Orléans is the exception: each player may build one station there.
answers.evidence: Building: Guildhall requires your Merchant in the town; occupied towns cannot receive another station; each player may build one in Orléans.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point, moving your marker one space. When Development movement lands on or passes a coin space, collect its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium; Scoring: coin, Citizen, and Development Status effects on moving onto or past spaces.

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two eligible Followers in one action. Starting marked Followers cannot be used. Send them to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions, including different Deeds; take each placement's depicted 1–3 coins, or for Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed's last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: one or both Followers; starting Followers barred; exact-profession free spaces; rewards and last-space Citizen.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5, the Action Phase. The other events resolve in Phase 6. The game opens with Pilgrimage because that tile is placed on top of the Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hour Glass/Event; Setup: Pilgrimage on top; Pilgrimage event rule applies before the Event Phase.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine qualify as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you have no food, you owe 5 coins; if you have fewer than five, you pay what you can and undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Events → Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; if unable, pay 5 coins; if unable to pay those coins, torture for shortfall; wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar is returned to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. The marked starting Trader is kept, so no Follower is lost and no replacement draw is made. You do not redraw a starting Follower.
answers.evidence: Events → Plague: neutral Follower returns to supply without track rollback; marked starting Follower is kept and no redraw occurs.

answers.answer: Pay the one coin you have, then replace each of the two missing coins with one eligible item per missing coin. Choices include a Trading Station, a random eligible neutral Follower from your bag, one Development Point, or a Goods, Place, or Technology tile. Marked starting Followers cannot be sacrificed; keep drawing and returning marked Followers until an eligible neutral one is drawn. A Development Point moves you one space left but never onto or past a coin space. Items surrendered are removed from the game; only lost Development Points can be regained.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy): available coins are paid; each missing coin replaced by a listed item; marked Followers protected; DP restriction; surrendered items removed.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part of that action would still give a reward. If goods or Followers return to supply through Harvest or Plague, the corresponding actions become available again. If the common coin supply is empty, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: cannot play an action providing an unavailable tile; Harvest/Plague may return goods/Followers and corresponding actions become available again; insufficient coin supply means no coins received.

answers.answer: A tie for most built Trading Stations means nobody takes the bonus Citizen. Final good values are grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, and brocade 5 points each. Final score is coins plus goods values plus (built Trading Stations + collected Citizens) multiplied by final Development Status. Ties go to the player further ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: unique most stations takes set-aside Citizen, tie gives nobody; goods values, scoring formula, and tie-break stated.
